target.title: fix(node-host): use surrogate-safe slice in truncateOutput to prevent ill-formed strings (fixes #99981)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`truncateOutput` in `src/node-host/invoke.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice` to keep the last `maxChars` (20,000) code units of captured exec output. When the truncation boundary falls inside a surrogate pair (e.g., emoji or CJK-extension characters), the result starts with a lone low surrogate (`\uDE00`), which is not valid Unicode. Downstream consumers — strict UTF-8 encoders, JSON transports, and DB drivers — either replace it with `\uFFFD` or reject the payload entirely.

The repo already has a surrogate-safe helper (`sliceUtf16Safe` in `src/shared/utf16-slice.ts`) used by sibling truncation helpers (`task-status.ts`, `tool-result-text.ts`, `exec-approval-command-display.ts`), but this call site did not use it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Single-line fix: replace `raw.slice(raw.length - maxChars)` with `sliceUtf16Safe(raw, raw.length - maxChars)` and add the import. The helper adjusts the slice start forward past a lone low surrogate (or the end backward past a lone high surrogate), so the returned string is always well-formed.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed:** Exec output truncation splitting surrogate pairs, producing ill-formed Unicode strings
- **Environment tested:** macOS, Node.js v22.22.3, OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (cf36cb9)
- **Steps run after the patch:**
  1. Built the project with `pnpm build`
  2. Verified the compiled bundle (`dist/node-cli-YmeB6Lsf.js`) uses `sliceUtf16Safe` in `truncateOutput`
  3. Tested with input `'😀a'.repeat(6667)` (20,001 code units, truncation boundary lands on a lone low surrogate)
  4. Ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/node-host/` — all 14 test files, 126 tests pass
- **Evidence after fix:**

```
=== OLD (raw.slice) ===
Content first char code: de00
Content well-formed: false

=== NEW (sliceUtf16Safe) ===
Content first char code: 61
Content well-formed: true
Content length: 19999

FIX VERIFIED: YES
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Truncated content starts at the next safe code-unit boundary (ASCII 'a' at code point 0x61) instead of a lone low surrogate. The string is well-formed Unicode.
- **What was not tested:** Live agent exec with >20k emoji output through a running gateway session (the function is an internal truncation helper exercised through the exec event path; the fix is verified at the function level against the compiled production bundle).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Exec output truncation splitting surrogate pairs, producing ill-formed Unicode strings
- **Environment tested:** macOS, Node.js v22.22.3, OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (cf36cb9)
- **Steps run after the patch:**
  1. Built the project with `pnpm build`
  2. Verified the compiled bundle (`dist/node-cli-YmeB6Lsf.js`) uses `sliceUtf16Safe` in `truncateOutput`
  3. Tested with input `'😀a'.repeat(6667)` (20,001 code units, truncation boundary lands on a lone low surrogate)
  4. Ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/node-host/` — all 14 test files, 126 tests pass
- **Evidence after fix:**

```
=== OLD (raw.slice) ===
Content first char code: de00
Content well-formed: false

=== NEW (sliceUtf16Safe) ===
Content first char code: 61
Content well-formed: true
Content length: 19999

FIX VERIFIED: YES
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Truncated content starts at the next safe code-unit boundary (ASCII 'a' at code point 0x61) instead of a lone low surrogate. The string is well-formed Unicode.
- **What was not tested:** Live agent exec with >20k emoji output through a running gateway session (the function is an internal truncation helper exercised through the exec event path; the fix is verified at the function level against the compiled production bundle).

## User Impact

Agents processing exec output containing emoji or CJK-extension characters will no longer produce corrupted strings when the output exceeds the 20,000-character truncation limit. Previously, the corrupted payload could cause downstream encoding failures or silent data loss via replacement characters.
